name: GSK5784283
summary: GSK5784283 (felcorekibart; formerly AIO-001 and Hengrui's SHR-1905) is a long-acting anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody. GSK got it when it bought Aiolos Bio (completed 14 February 2024; $1bn upfront plus up to $400mm in milestones). GSK holds the rights outside Greater China and owes Hengrui milestones and tiered royalties. Phase 3 PERSIST programme: asthma NCT07780643 and NCT07782996 (primary completion 2029-02-15 and 2029-05-04), COPD NCT07780669 and NCT07780656 (2029-07-20, eosinophilic phenotype, on triple or dual therapy), CRSwNP NCT07782957 and NCT07782970 (2029-03-06). The price anchor is Tezspire (tezepelumab), the only marketed anti-TSLP, at $29,549 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024. The uptake anchor is Tezspire's measured capture of the US asthma biologic class, taken at half for a second-in-class entrant, the multiple the book uses for tilrekimig.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07780643, NCT07780669 (ClinicalTrials.gov): add-on maintenance antibody vs placebo on top of standard care, exacerbation endpoints
therapy_mode.note: A maintenance biologic in asthma and COPD, continued while it works. The dosing interval is not published, so it is not claimed here

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Tezspire: CMS Part D 2024, $183,765,288 over 6,219 beneficiaries = $29,549 per beneficiary. Part B 2024 agrees at $28,676 ($218,453,021 over 7,618)
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. Tezspire is the only marketed drug with this mechanism, in the same diseases and route, and the book already prices tozorakimab off the same row, so the two stay consistent. In GBP, the currency the book's other GSK seeds use: $29,549 at GBP/USD 1.327632 (the rate gsk_efimosfermin_alfa.csv and gsk_mrna_seasonal_flu.csv use) is GBP 22,257 (0.022257 mm GBP). The case against: (1) a per-beneficiary figure covers part of a year, so it understates a full year. tezspire.com states a list price of $4,587.41 per 210 mg syringe (seen through search, not opened), about $59,636 a year at 13 doses. (2) If felcorekibart is dosed less often, GSK may price it at Exdensur (depemokimab), its own twice-yearly asthma biologic. Its US WAC was not found; drugs.com shows a cash price of about $25,405 a dose. (3) Nucala runs $35,081 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand)

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention: halving a CMS per-beneficiary figure lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices (backend/gross_to_net.py); the same row tozorakimab carries on the same Tezspire anchor
gross_to_net_pct.note: Net is 50% of list, about $14,775 a patient-year. The case against: the tilrekimig seed measures 26% off for Dupixent (ICER AD report 2021, SSR Health). On that figure, net would be $21,866

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: reused from the tilrekimig seed (pfe_tilrekimig.csv): Symons JM et al., J Drugs Dermatol 2025;24(10):996-1002, 55.7% of dupilumab starters persistent at 24 months, a constant 25.4% stopping a year. Tozorakimab carries 0.254 for respiratory biologics on the same basis
discontinuation_pct.note: JUDGEMENT to reuse it. It is the book's respiratory-biologic rate, but it was measured in atopic dermatitis, not asthma. A longer dosing interval could lower it; no persistence data exist for this asset

forecast_start_year.source: earliest Phase 3 primary completion is NCT07780643 (asthma), 2029-02-15; CRSwNP 2029-03-06, second asthma trial 2029-05-04, COPD 2029-07-20 (trials in context file)
forecast_start_year.note: Filing in the second half of 2029 and a standard BLA review put launch in the second half of 2030, so 2031 is the first full year. That follows the book's pipeline rule of two calendar years after primary completion, as tilrekimig does. The case against: the programme is recruiting or not yet recruiting, and any enrolment slip moves this back

exus_multiple.source: GSK's own respiratory biologic Nucala, FY2025: GBP 521mm Europe plus GBP 447mm International against GBP 1,040mm US (asset_revenue_regions, annual report table 0001654954-26-000892) = 968 / 1,040
exus_multiple.note: Felcorekibart excludes Greater China, where Hengrui keeps the rights, while Nucala's International includes China, so the multiple leans slightly high. Tezspire's AstraZeneca-booked ex-US (Europe $297mm, Established ROW $121mm, EM $40mm in FY2025) has no matching AZ-booked US figure on file, so it cannot be used as a ratio

economics_share.source: GSK press release 'GSK completes acquisition of Aiolos Bio' (14 February 2024, https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/gsk-completes-acquisition-of-aiolos-bio/) and 6-K 0001654954-24-000339: GSK owns the asset and holds the rights outside Greater China, and is responsible for success-based milestones and tiered royalties owed to Jiangsu Hengrui
economics_share.note: JUDGEMENT. GSK books all ex-China sales, so revenue share is 1.0. The case against: the tiered royalty to Hengrui is not disclosed. It is a real cost this row does not net, so the value is a ceiling. Up to $400mm of regulatory milestones to Aiolos holders, and further Hengrui milestones, sit outside these rows

prevalence.note: lookup.py pool Asthma: 23,004,000 US adults with current asthma (CDC NHIS 2023), on the tilrekimig seed

incidence.note: lookup.py pool Asthma: 906,458 a year (Winer RA et al., J Asthma 2012), on the tilrekimig seed

eligible_pct.source: Akenroye A, McCormack M, Keet C. J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020;145(4):1295-1297: 2.8% of adults with current asthma eligible for at least one asthma biologic (the book's asthma row, lookup.py pool)
eligible_pct.note: PERSIST ASTHMA enrols uncontrolled asthma as add-on therapy. Tezspire's label has no phenotype or biomarker limit, so the all-biologic-eligible share fits a TSLP antibody. Kept identical to tilrekimig so the two draw on one pool

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Tezspire's measured class capture: 13,837 Medicare Part B plus D beneficiaries in 2024, 16.94% of the 81,661 across Tezspire, Nucala, Fasenra and Xolair (drug_demand; figures as the tozorakimab and tilrekimig seeds cite them). Park J et al., J Asthma Allergy 2026;19:1-12: 11.9% of type 2 severe asthma patients on a biologic. Half of 16.94% x 11.9% = 1.008% of the eligible pool on therapy
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: the 0.5 multiple. It is solved back through the engine's own identity (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock) on the book's asthma pool, this curve and 25.37% discontinuation, so the stock reaches 1.008% of the eligible pool in the third year (index 2). 2024 was Tezspire's third full year. The multiple is the one tilrekimig uses: a second TSLP arrives in 2031 against Tezspire, Exdensur and a crowded class. The case against: a less frequent dose could win more than half the incumbent's pace (at 1.0x the peak would be about 0.0142). Verekitug (Upstream Bio, TSLP receptor, every 12 weeks, Phase 2 VALIANT) is a further in-class entrant

ramp_steepness.source: Tezspire's own launch fitted by the tilrekimig seed: CMS Part B plus D beneficiaries 3,962, 8,973 and 13,837 over 2022 to 2024, logistic k 1.28 with midpoint 0.96 years
ramp_steepness.note: reused from the closest modelled competitor curve, the same mechanism in the same disease

ramp_midpoint_year.note: Unshifted because asthma is this asset's lead indication and sets the 2031 start. Tilrekimig shifts it by one year only because its asthma line is later than its lead

prevalence.note: epidemiology.csv: 14.2mm US adults with diagnosed COPD (CDC BRFSS)

incidence.note: epidemiology.csv carries no COPD incidence. The only book row is tozorakimab's, set equal to prevalence (carryover zero). The peak below is solved on that treatment, and it moves less than 1% if carryover is instead 1.0 with no inflow (0.00779 against 0.00775)

eligible_pct.source: GSK release 2025-05-22 (Nucala COPD approval), cited in the book's COPD eligible row: over a million US COPD patients uncontrolled on inhaled triple therapy who keep exacerbating have blood eosinophils of 150 cells/uL or above. 1,000,000 / 14,200,000 = 0.0704
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the threshold. PERSIST COPD-1 (NCT07780669, via AdisInsight and the trial record) enrols an eosinophilic phenotype with elevated blood eosinophils, frequent exacerbations and triple (or dual if ICS is inappropriate) therapy, so the book's all-eosinophil 0.1006 (tozorakimab) is too wide. The exact eosinophil cut-off was not visible. If it is 300 cells/uL, as in Dupixent's COPD label, the pool is smaller

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: the same anchor as asthma: half of Tezspire's measured capture, 0.5 x 16.94% x 11.9% = 1.008% on therapy by the third year, which is how tozorakimab takes Tezspire into COPD (at 1.0x)
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: the 0.5 multiple and an asthma analogue in COPD. Solved through forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock on 14.2mm x 0.0704, carryover zero, the curve below and 25.37% discontinuation. Tezspire has no COPD label. The COPD incumbents Dupixent (2024) and Nucala (May 2025) launched too recently for a measured curve. Tozorakimab reads 2.02% at 1.0x with a slower curve

ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT to apply an asthma launch curve to COPD. Tozorakimab uses the book's average launch (k 0.53, midpoint 1.75), which is slower

ramp_midpoint_year.note: COPD completes 2029-07-20, five months after the asthma lead, so it is assumed to file with it and is not shifted. If it is filed as a later supplement, add about a year
